document.executive_summary: This memo recomputes the WO-01 pump-module decision independently from the trusted source table and cross-checks the proposal author's report against it. All four candidates pass both policy gates, so qualification is unanimous. On the shared acceptance-run basis the verified energy order is P2 at 12 kWh, P3 at 52, P1 at 56 and P4 at 58, giving gaps to the winner of 40, 44 and 46 kWh. P2 clears both gates with the field's highest quality (97) and one defect. The author's gate arithmetic, ranking, gap figures and policy reading all reproduce exactly from the table; no invented measurements were found. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified and stay excluded. My independent ballot is P2.
document.figure_caption: Verification diagram: gate status and measured energy per candidate, with dashed gap markers showing computed shortfalls of 40, 44 and 46 kWh to P2 on the common basis.

recommendation.rationale: P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying candidate: 12 kWh against 52 (P3), 56 (P1) and 58 (P4) on an identical acceptance-run basis. It clears both gates with the highest quality index (97) and one defect, and its 40–46 kWh advantage dominates any plausible single-run measurement nuance. Unverified cost or reliability data cannot enter under the written

sections.body: The policy requires a quality index of at least 80, at most five raw defects, and then the lowest energy among qualifiers. From the trusted table: P2 at quality 97 with one defect; P1 at 84 with four; P4 at 81 with zero; P3 at exactly 80 with three. All four clear the quality floor — P3 with no headroom — and all sit inside the defect ceiling. Qualification is unanimous, so reject_all does not apply and no candidate is removed on gate grounds.
sections.heading: Gate Recomputation from the Trusted Table

sections.body: All energy values share the same output, load and acceptance-run basis, so the column is directly comparable. The verified order is P2 at 12 kWh, P3 at 52, P1 at 56 and P4 at 58. Recomputed gaps to the winner: P3 52−12 = 40 kWh; P1 56−12 = 44 kWh; P4 58−12 = 46 kWh. Even substantial uncertainty in a single run could not plausibly close a 40 kWh spread, so the ordering is robust on the supplied facts.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic

sections.body: The author's report reproduces the trusted table correctly and states the shared-basis caveat; I find no invented measurements. The claim that quality and defects act only as gates is a correct reading of the written policy, and the note that P4's zero-defect record would matter only under an unissued weighting rule is clearly labeled hypothetical, not asserted as fact. The executive figures (12/52/56/58, gaps 40/44/46) match my recomputation line for line. I record no factual error in the delivered report.
sections.heading: Cross-Check of the Proposal Author's Claims

sections.body: Unverified by the supplied data: unit cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability; no weighting beyond quality, defects and energy is supplied, so none may enter the ranking. For C's handover: confirm the gate arithmetic, the energy figures and the gap values against the trusted table; log any client clarification before award; treat P4's zero-defect profile as an open reliability question, not a scoring input. My P2 ballot is my own judgment from the table, not an endorsement of the author's text.
